newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds up amid positive global sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds up amid positive global sentiment.

text.p: Irish bonds strengthened in thin late trade on Tuesday in line with international markets on the back of very positive global sentiment, dealers said.
Dealers said a close eye is still likely to be kept on the U.S. amid speculation that a rise in interest rates might be announced when the Federal Open Market Committe (FOMC) next meets.
Tuesday's crucial U.S. inflation and retail sales data had soothed fears of an early rise in interest rates and boosted U.S. treasury bonds, dealers said.
"The Irish market is in pretty good shape. Global markets have done very well today and that has given us a push," Riada's Padraig Garvey said.

"The punt is near recent highs versus the mark and that has supported the short-end while we have also seen an easing in the money market situation with the Irish Central Bank selling off of the punt in recent days.
"We have seen good overseas and domestic interest in the Irish market along the curve, which has steepened up with the short-end out-performing the longer-end," he added.

By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had gained 40 pence from Monday's close to 102.05 to yield 5.89 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 had risen 45 pence from the close to 109.15 to yield 6.56 percent.
Irish bonds were trading at 160 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area and at 89 basis points over bunds in the 10-year area.
